lede: Raising β blurs the digit and turns unused latent axes off. Diversity peaks at β = 1, not at the Optuna pick.
title: β-VAE on digits
question: What does the KL weight do to reconstruction, active latent axes, and sample diversity?
process: This is the same _vae_loss as the comparison VAE. β is the only new coefficient, and it multiplies the KL, not the pixels:

A traversal does not retrain. It starts at the zero code and moves one coordinate from −3 to 3 while decode draws the image. An active axis is one whose posterior mean still varies across the test set, variance above 0.01.

Optuna, with every other setting fixed, scored β = 0.1, 1, 4, 10 at validation losses 100.4, 117.8, 152.0, and 189.5. The 10-epoch sweep puts the diversity peak at β = 1 (0.226) and the sharpest test MSE at β = 0.1 (0.091).

opening.summary: Two bold points, two objectives. Optuna picks β = 0.1. The panels pick β = 1 for diversity. Hover a β to swap the traversal.

charts.title: Test MSE, active axes, and diversity

marks.summary: β = 0.1 has the sharpest reconstructions in the sweep (test MSE 0.0907) and all 8 axes stay active. Per-axis KL sits in a narrow band, about 3.1 to 3.8. Every traversal row changes the digit. Diversity is 0.168, tighter than β = 1. Optuna picks this β because it minimizes the weighted loss, which is the best reconstruction here and not the most compact code.
marks.frameCaption: β = 0.1. Every row still changes the digit.

marks.summary: β = 1 is bold on these panels because diversity peaks here at 0.226. Test MSE rises only to 0.0940, all 8 axes stay active, and KL falls to 15.03. The traversal rows still change the glyph. Optuna does not pick this point. It picks β = 0.1, where the weighted validation loss is lower and the samples are tighter.
marks.frameCaption: β = 1. Every row still moves the glyph.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: β = 4 pushes test MSE to 0.1114 and KL down to 8.37. Active units fall to 7. One axis, z4, has KL about 0.007 and a traversal response near zero. Diversity slips to 0.204. The code is getting smaller by switching an axis off, and the digits are blurrier.
marks.frameCaption: β = 4. Rows still move, and the digits are blurrier.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: β = 10 is the blurriest decoder (test MSE 0.1480) and the least diverse prior (0.151). KL is 3.94. z3, z4, and z5 each have KL under 0.02 and their traversal rows barely move: three rows of the grid stay a single glyph. The rows that still move still change which digit you see. That is unused axes turning off, not one axis owning slant. MNIST does not label a continuous factor, so the grid is not a disentanglement claim.
marks.frameCaption: β = 10. Several rows stay one smeared digit.

marks.summary: β = 0.1 is bold because Optuna minimizes the β-weighted validation loss and this trial scores 100.37. Hidden size, dropout, learning rate, weight decay, batch size, and latent size were the same on every trial, so the bar isolates β. best_params.json stores this value. It is the best reconstruction weight in the search, and it is the low-diversity end of the sweep.
marks.frameCaption: β = 0.1. Every row still changes the digit.

marks.summary: β = 1 scores validation loss 117.77. The weighted objective is worse than at 0.1, and the exploration sweep says this is where diversity peaks. The search and the sample grid want different β.
marks.frameCaption: β = 1. Every row still moves the glyph.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: β = 4 scores validation loss 151.98. In the longer sweep, test MSE is 0.1114, active units fall to 7, and one traversal row goes quiet. The objective and the pictures agree that the code is being squeezed.
marks.frameCaption: β = 4. Rows still move, and the digits are blurrier.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: β = 10 is the worst Optuna loss, 189.53, and the blurriest sweep point, test MSE 0.1480, diversity 0.151, six active axes. z3, z4, and z5 have KL under 0.02 and their traversal rows barely move. The frozen rows are unused axes. MNIST does not label a continuous factor, so the grid is not a disentanglement claim.
marks.frameCaption: β = 10. Several rows stay one smeared digit.

reflection.worked: Measured: Optuna’s lowest weighted loss is β = 0.1 at 100.37, and that sweep point has test MSE 0.0907 with all 8 axes active. Diversity peaks at β = 1, at 0.226. The traversal shows which row moves.
reflection.unexpected: Measured: the search picks the reconstruction weight, not the diverse one. At β = 10, three traversal rows freeze and only six axes stay active.
reflection.why: Measured: β is the multiplier on the KL, and the active-unit count is a variance threshold of 0.01. Guess, and not a disentanglement result: MNIST has no labeled factor such as slant, so a frozen row is unused capacity rather than a discovered factor.
reflection.improve: Put diversity next to the Optuna loss, or the search will keep choosing a small β. Keep β near 1 when the goal is the sample grid. Use a dataset with known factors if the claim is disentanglement.
